boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus places that support studying, recreation, events, performances, or quiet breaks, documented by Rose-Hulman sources.

cards.title: Mussallem Union
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for dining, recreation, and services
cards.notes: Use the social spaces for a study break or a game of pool, foosball, or giant Connect 4; dining and campus-service offices are in the same building.
cards.short_summary: A central indoor stop that combines gathering space, dining, recreation, and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman describes the Mussallem Union as a campus hub with social spaces, recreation, dining options, and offices including Student Affairs and Counseling Services.
cards.access_notes: Campus building; consult the Union room guide or campus staff for room access and event availability.

cards.title: Pi-Vilion
cards.subtitle: Glass-enclosed pavilion beside Mussallem Union
cards.notes: Look for the glass pavilion beside the Union and its visible green roof; it is designed for events and student gatherings, so confirm availability before planning one.
cards.short_summary: An event-ready pavilion that is visually distinct from the adjacent student union.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman identifies the Pi-Vilion as a glass-enclosed pavilion adjacent to Mussallem Union, with seating for 40–50 and use for presentations, movie nights, and other gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Event space; availability and use are subject to scheduling.

cards.title: John A. Logan Library
cards.subtitle: Library in the heart of campus
cards.notes: Set up in one of the library’s welcoming study areas, then use the service desk for materials or research help when you need a focused academic reset.
cards.short_summary: A campus-centered library with study space, information resources, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman says Logan Library provides high-quality information resources, welcoming study spaces, and services that support student learning.
cards.access_notes: Library services are intended for the Rose-Hulman community; check current building access and service hours.

cards.title: The Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Logan Library
cards.notes: Bring a course question, a review packet, or a small group to the lower level of Logan Library; tutors are available with or without an appointment.
cards.short_summary: Peer tutoring, review support, and quiet study areas in Logan Library’s lower level.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Center offers individual and small-group tutoring, review sessions, quiet study areas, and course materials, and is located in the lower level of Logan Library.
cards.access_notes: Rose-Hulman lists tutor availability Monday–Friday 9:00 a.m.–4:50 p.m. and Sunday–Thursday 7:00–10:00 p.m.; verify current schedules.

cards.title: Chapman Root Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Grassy quad among academic buildings and Logan Library
cards.notes: Use the lawn as an outdoor pause between classes or a place to read when conditions allow; it sits among academic buildings and the library.
cards.short_summary: A named open lawn at the center of daily movement between academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman describes the Quad as a grassy area between surrounding academic buildings and Logan Library that can be used for an occasional game or relaxing study.
cards.source_title: Top 15 Instagram-worthy Spots on Campus | Rose-Hulman
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; use is weather-dependent and events may affect availability.

cards.title: Speed Lake
cards.subtitle: Campus lake by Speed Hall
cards.notes: Walk the lake edge for a short break and photograph the water from campus paths; keep recreation within posted conditions and any institute guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named campus landmark beside residence life and outdoor pathways.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman identifies Speed Lake as a campus landmark where students may take a break from studies and participate in activities such as fishing or ice skating when conditions permit.
cards.source_title: Top 15 Instagram-worthy Spots on Campus | Rose-Hulman
cards.access_notes: Use shoreline paths and follow posted safety guidance; water and ice activities depend on conditions and authorization.

cards.title: White Chapel
cards.subtitle: Lakeside space for worship and spiritual refuge
cards.notes: Visit the chapel’s lakeside exterior for a quiet pause; ask the appropriate campus contact before entering or arranging any group use.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive lakeside chapel used for worship, services, cultural events, and alumni weddings.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman describes White Chapel as a space for worship and spiritual refuge overlooking the lake, used for established campus-group services and available to outside groups as scheduling permits.
cards.access_notes: The university states that outside-group use is available as scheduling permits; confirm entry and reservation arrangements.

cards.title: Moench Hall
cards.subtitle: Main academic building on the south side of Speed Lake
cards.notes: Use this as the landmark for academic departments and labs, then pause at the lake-side approach before heading into your next scheduled class or meeting.
cards.short_summary: Rose-Hulman’s main academic building, with departments, classrooms, and laboratories.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s campus map identifies Moench Hall as the main academic building and lists engineering, science, computing, and humanities departments along with advanced learning environments.
cards.access_notes: Academic building; classroom and laboratory access may be limited to authorized students, staff, and scheduled visitors.

cards.title: Hatfield Hall
cards.subtitle: Theater, performing-arts, and alumni-history building
cards.notes: Check the performance calendar, then look for the theater and alumni center; this is a useful named stop when you want a campus arts or history connection.
cards.short_summary: A campus building that brings together theater, music studios, performing arts, and alumni history.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman states that Hatfield Hall includes a 602-seat theater for student performances and a performing arts series, an alumni center with historical artifacts, and music studio rooms.
cards.source_title: Top 15 Instagram-worthy Spots on Campus | Rose-Hulman
cards.access_notes: Performance and interior access vary by event and building operations; consult the current arts calendar or campus office.

cards.title: SRC Bouldering Wall
cards.subtitle: Sports and Recreation Center climbing facility
cards.notes: Ask SRC staff about current use procedures and supervision, then try a beginner-appropriate route or observe the wall as part of a recreation-center visit.
cards.short_summary: A supervised indoor bouldering facility with features for different experience levels.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman says the SRC Bouldering Wall has varied climbing features, accommodates beginners through advanced climbers, and is supervised by SRC staff while in use.
cards.source_title: Sports & Recreation Center – Facilities & Hours | Rose-Hulman
cards.access_notes: Located in the SRC; the university states staff supervise the wall while it is in use. Confirm eligibility and current facility hours.
